title: Decision 0008: signalman is a tool for agents, not an agent
description:
Write docs/decisions/0008-signalman-is-a-tool-for-agents.md from the template, status accepted, and link it from docs/decisions/README.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md.

Context: the Cersei evaluation recorded on the parent epic (signalman-4gp), and the recurring question "should signalman investigate or remediate on its own".

Considered options: (1) embed an agentic loop (Cersei or similar) inside the triage path; (2) expose signalman's typed capabilities to external agents over MCP and a stable JSON contract, with no generative model in the binary; (3) do nothing.

Outcome: option 2. Consequences: the deterministic core and decisions 0001 and 0002 hold; a generative model may appear only in offline tooling outside the triage path and never writes to incident.io; every capability an agent can call is one signalman already exposes in the CLI.

Confirmation: Cargo.toml carries no LLM SDK dependency; the MCP tool list is generated from the same code paths as the CLI subcommands; a test asserts the write tool is absent when mcp.allow_write is false.

Revisit criteria, stated in the record: a responder need that cannot be decomposed into deterministic retrieval plus a typed question; live verification (signalman-b11) complete; a human approval channel in incident.io (workflow or decision flow) that signalman can wait on.
acceptance_criteria: ADR 0008 merged with frontmatter, linked from the decisions index, architecture and roadmap; CLAUDE.md rule added: no generative-model SDK in the triage path, agents call signalman over MCP.

title: Change feed adapters: Argo CD and GitLab webhooks in their native shapes
description:
The change feed (decision 0007) takes signalman's own JSON, which asks every pipeline to write a template. Two sources cover most deploys here and both can post their native payload: Argo CD notifications can send the Application object ({{ toJson .app }}), and GitLab project webhooks send documented event payloads with X-Gitlab-Event and X-Gitlab-Token headers.

Add two adapter endpoints that translate into Change and record it:
- POST /changes/argocd: an Argo CD Application (or {app, context}); component = metadata.name; kind deploy; summary from the last history entry or operationState (revision, destination namespace, images, initiator); at = history.deployedAt or operationState.finishedAt; url = context.argocdUrl/applications/<name> when the context is posted. Bearer token as the plain feed.
- POST /changes/gitlab: X-Gitlab-Token compared in constant time against the feed token; X-Gitlab-Event decides the mapping: Deployment Hook (status success only) -> deploy; Feature Flag Hook -> flag; Release Hook -> release; Merge Request Hook (action merge) -> merge. Other events answer 200 ignored. component = project.name lowercased.

Wire types lenient (unknown fields ignored). Fixtures from the official docs under examples/changes/. Tests per adapter plus router tests. docs/changes.md documents both setups; the generic endpoint stays.
close_reason: POST /changes/argocd (Application object, bearer) and POST /changes/gitlab (X-Gitlab-Token, X-Gitlab-Event: Deployment success, Feature Flag, Release create, Merge Request merge) translate native payloads into changes; failed syncs and non-change events answer 200 ignored; fixtures from the documented payloads under examples/changes; unit and router tests; docs/changes.md documents both setups.

title: Layered configuration: file, environment, command line
description:
The binary is configured by environment variables and a few flags, read in six different places. That works for one laptop and breaks in Kubernetes, where shape (URLs, thresholds, rubric text, team list) belongs in a ConfigMap under review, secrets belong in a Secret, and an operator needs to know which value won.

Deliver one configuration model with an explicit precedence, lowest to highest: built-in default, configuration file (TOML), environment variable, command-line flag. Every environment read moves into one module so the precedence table in the docs is the code. Secrets (API keys, tokens, webhook secret) are never accepted from the file.

Also move what was compiled but is really configuration into the file: policy thresholds, the fallback team list, the impact rubric, and the text of every question. The set of questions and their types stay in code: the policy consumes them and the typed handles exist to keep that contract honest.

title: Related firing alerts as blast-radius context
description:
An alert is qualified faster when the responder and the model see what else is firing. Fetch firing alerts created within a window (GET /v2/alerts?status[one_of]=firing&created_at[gte]=<now-window>, page_size 50), exclude the alert itself, cap the list (20), and add them to the state as alert.related_alerts with title, age in minutes and the component label when present. Reference the path in the impact question guidance (several alerts on the same component or its dependents indicate broader impact) and in the dedup question. List them in the qualification note.

Observability alerts from Tsuga reach this list through Tsuga's native incident.io notification integration; no Tsuga client is added (decision 0005).

title: Qualification note on the incident.io alert
description:
Tags encode the verdict but not the reasoning, the confidence, or where to look next. A responder still opens Backstage, the runbook and the incident list by hand. Post one markdown note on the alert (POST /v1/alert_notes, alert_id) that carries everything the tags imply plus what they cannot: owner with confidence and the confirm-owner flag, impact level with its distribution, actionable probability, the matched incident with permalink, suspected change, the resolved catalog component and owner group as Backstage links, the TechDocs runbook page link, the upstream alert link, related firing alerts, and the time to qualify.

Rules: deterministic template in code (decision 0002: no generated text). Exactly one signalman note per alert: list existing notes (GET /v1/alert_notes?alert_id=) and PUT the existing one when its first line carries the signalman marker, so retriage rewrites in place instead of stacking. Respect WriteBack::DryRun. A note failure is logged and must not undo tags or attachments. Backstage links need BACKSTAGE_APP_URL (frontend), defaulting to BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL.

Acceptance: wiremock test asserts the note body and the create-or-replace behaviour; Outcome gains note_id; docs updated (incident.io page, configuration).

title: Reduce mean time to qualify (MTTQ)
description:
Mean time to qualify: the time from an alert being created in incident.io to the moment a responder has, in one place, the answers to five questions: is it actionable, who owns it, how bad is it, is it already a known incident, and did something change. signalman already computes those judgments; the gap is that they surface only as tags, without the reasoning, the links or the surrounding context, and that nobody measures the interval.

Scope, deliberately small (Unix rule: few things, done well):
1. One qualification note on the alert in incident.io, rewritten in place, with judgments, links (incident, Backstage component and owner group, TechDocs runbook, upstream alert) and the time to qualify.
2. Other firing alerts in the window as blast-radius context, in the model state and in the note.
3. Time to qualify measured per alert (alert created_at to decision) in the outcome, logs and note.
4. Decision record: observability signals (Tsuga) enter through incident.io; no direct Tsuga client until the spec is verified with an operation API key.

Out of scope, recorded as deferred children: on-call lookup through incident.io schedules; a direct Tsuga client.

title: Retry parity, stated: retry-after-ms and HTTP-date Retry-After, one-sided jitter, opt-in total budget, a conservative() preset; rustdoc says what matches the SDK and what does not
description:
S3 of the 7v9 plan (judgment 0.2.0). All code in crates/judgment/src/http.rs, which stays generic.
Bug: parse_retry_after panicked on Retry-After inf/infinity/1e20 (Duration::from_secs_f64); now ignored.
RetryPolicy gains http_statuses (default {408,429} + 500..=599), transport: TransportRetry (non_exhaustive; Any default, BeforeSend = reqwest is_connect only, Never) and budget: Option<Duration> (default None). Struct stays constructible (struct update). is_retryable is a &self method; retries_transport(&reqwest::Error). conservative() = {408,429}, BeforeSend.
Jitter only subtracts: delay = exp - exp*U*j, j clamped to [0,1], NaN -> 0, no mul_f64 panic on Duration::MAX.
Budget (tenacity stop_before_delay): counts attempts and waits from the first send; elapsed + next delay >= budget returns the last failure with a warn 'retry budget spent; returning the last failure'. Some(ZERO) = no retries. Never cuts an attempt in flight.
Server wait: retry-after-ms > Retry-After seconds > HTTP date (IMF-fixdate, RFC 850, asctime, measured against the response Date header when it parses, else now; past = 0); non-finite/huge/negative ignored; empty ignored. Honoured on any retryable status up to retry_after_max.
Cargo: workspace httpdate = 1; judgment optional httpdate in the http feature. Re-export TransportRetry from client and lib.
Rustdoc: each field at its extremes, the server wait, the budget, parity with Python 0.7.1 and JS 0.6.0 (matches, deliberately differs, not implemented). Replace SDK-equivalent/mirror claims (Cargo description, lib.rs, client.rs, http.rs, README, src/lib.rs, docs/typesafe-client.md).
Consumers: fast_retries literals in crates/judgment/tests/client.rs and tests/incidentio.rs gain ..RetryPolicy::default(); http.rs retry_after_header_parses_seconds_only deleted and folded into retry_after_forms_and_precedence.
Tests: unit backoff/jitter/statuses/budget/retry-after forms/hostile values; wiremock retry-after-ms, budget, conservative (5xx, 429, timeout, refused connection), transport Never, truncated body over a raw TCP server; RetryPolicy struct-update doctest.
Docs: roadmap (HTTP-date gap), incidentio.md, architecture.md, operations.md (budget warn log), development.md (doctests), CHANGELOG Fixed/Added/Changed/Breaking; regenerate docs/llms*.txt.
Commit: judgment: retry-after-ms, HTTP-date waits, one-sided jitter, opt-in budget and conservative() (7v9.5)

A new subcommand `signalman mcp` serves the Model Context Protocol over stdio (Streamable HTTP later, mounted on the existing axum router when a bearer token is configured). Tools, all read-only, each a thin wrapper over the code the CLI subcommand already calls so there is exactly one implementation per capability:
- qualify_alert(alert_id | alert JSON): full triage in dry-run mode; returns the Outcome contract (schema v1) with every probability, the decision and the links. Writes nothing.
- related_alerts(alert_id | component, window_minutes): the blast-radius list the flow computes.
- recent_changes(component?, window_minutes): matches from the in-process ChangeLog (empty when the feed is not configured, with a reason).
- lookup_owner(component | alert text): Backstage resolution, candidates and the runbook page.
- open_incidents(): the dedup candidate list.
Each tool has an input schema from schemars, a one-paragraph description written for a model (what it answers, what it never does), and returns structured content plus a short text fallback.

Rules carried over: never creates incidents (decision 0001); no generative model anywhere (decisions 0002 and 0008); secrets stay env-only; configuration under a new [mcp] table (enabled, transport, bind address) with rows in docs/configuration.md and env vars in ENV_VARS.

Observability: one tracing span per tool call carrying the tool name, duration and whether it failed, so signalman-m28.2 exports it with the rest.

Docs: docs/mcp.md with a Claude Code `.mcp.json` example and an incident.io assistant note; mkdocs nav; README feature line.

title: Runbook section suggestion as a typed Choice in the qualification note
description:
The investigation people expect from an "agent" on an alert is mostly: open the runbook, find the step that matches this failure. signalman already retrieves the runbook excerpt from TechDocs (src/backstage/enrich.rs, alert.runbook, one page capped at 1,800 characters) and puts it in the state. Deliver the step selection as a typed question, no agent loop.

Design:
- Split the excerpt deterministically on Markdown headings into sections; keep heading, anchor and the first sentence. Sections are options for a Choice question "Which runbook section applies to this alert" with a no-match option, referencing `alert.runbook_sections` by path. Ask only when there are at least two sections (the model cannot choose what is not offered).
- Policy: surface the chosen section only above a confidence threshold in Policy (default conservative); below it the note says no section matched.
- Note: one line under the runbook link: the section title as a deep link (TechDocs anchor), with its probability. Fixed template, no prose from the model.
- Outcome: `runbook_section` in the JSON contract (signalman-4gp child "Stable JSON contract").
- Eval: add expected.runbook_section to the case format as optional; grade it when present.

Load the typesafe:typesafe-ai skill and use the question-designer agent before writing the question. Live TechDocs verification (signalman-b11.5) should run before trusting the section split on a real backend.

title: Stable JSON contract for the triage outcome (schema v1)
description:

Scope:
- An `Outcome` wire type with `schema_version: 1`, stable snake_case names, every optional field present as null, probabilities as numbers in [0,1], the decision as an enum string, related alerts and recent changes as arrays of typed objects, links as URLs, and time_to_qualify_seconds.
- Emit it from every `--json` path and from the webhook outcome log line, so the CLI, the server log and the future MCP server share one shape.
- Generate the JSON Schema with schemars into docs/schema/outcome.v1.json and a test that fails when the emitted shape drifts from the committed schema.
- Document it in docs/triage.md (or a new docs/contract.md) with one full example.

Non-goals: no change to the qualification note template; no change to the TypeSafe request shape.

title: Agent interoperability: signalman as a tool for agents, not an agent
description:
Cersei (github.com/pacifio/cersei, crates.io 0.2.6, MIT) was evaluated on 2026-09-22 as a way to give signalman agent capabilities. It is a Rust SDK for coding agents: a generative-LLM agentic loop (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Vertex) that decides which tools to call, plus sub-agents, file/shell/web tools, memory tiers, skills, an MCP client and a serialisable workflow engine.

Not adopted, for three reasons.

1. Thesis mismatch. Decision 0002 says no model generates text anywhere in signalman: deterministic logic in code, the model answers narrow typed questions. An agentic loop is the opposite: the model chooses actions and writes prose. Decision 0001 bounds writes to incident.io to tags, attachments and one note. An agent with tools inside the triage path would need both decisions reopened.

2. Weight. cersei-tools pulls five tree-sitter grammars, tantivy, nix, an LSP client and an embeddings crate; cersei-agent pulls memory, MCP and compression; the whole tree uses reqwest 0.12 and chrono where signalman uses reqwest 0.13 and jiff, so the binary would carry two HTTP stacks. signalman has about sixteen direct dependencies today.

3. Maturity. Single maintainer, 0.2.x with in-code notes of removed APIs, 700 crates.io downloads, no MSRV. Its abstractions (working directory, session, CLAUDE.md memory) are shaped for a coding CLI, not a service.

What responders and their tooling actually need is the inverse: signalman's typed judgments callable from agents they already use (Claude Code, Claude in Slack, incident.io's own assistant, internal copilots). That keeps the deterministic core and makes signalman a building block. Children, in order: a decision record; a stable JSON contract for the outcome; a read-only MCP server over the existing capabilities; an opt-in write tool; llms.txt for the docs; and a deferred record for agent-driven remediation so the question is not reopened without its criteria.

The one place agent-style investigation adds MTTQ value, choosing the runbook section that applies, is delivered as a typed question under signalman-3l7 instead.

title: MCP write tool apply_qualification behind mcp.allow_write (default off)
description:
Once an agent has seen a qualify_alert result and a human has agreed, let it ask signalman to apply that exact result: tags, the qualification note rewritten in place, and the incident attachment when the decision says so. This is the same write path the webhook flow uses; the tool adds nothing the flow cannot already do and never creates an incident (decision 0001).

Design:
- Input is the Outcome the agent received (schema v1) plus the alert id, not free parameters: signalman re-derives the writes from the typed answers, so the agent cannot invent a tag or a note line.
- Guard: the tool is registered only when mcp.allow_write is true (file or SIGNALMAN_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE); a test asserts it is absent otherwise. Note text stays the fixed template; the agent's name and the MCP client id are recorded in the outcome log, never in the note.
- Idempotent: applying the same Outcome twice is a no-op on tags and replaces the note in place.

title: Agent-driven remediation: deferred until its criteria are met
description:
Recorded so the question is not reopened from scratch. Executing runbook steps (rollbacks, restarts, scaling) from signalman, whether by an embedded agent SDK such as Cersei or by a hand-written loop, is out of scope until all of the following hold:

1. Decision 0008 is revisited with a responder need that cannot be met by deterministic retrieval plus a typed question plus an external agent calling signalman over MCP.
2. Live verification (signalman-b11) is complete and the harness (signalman eval) shows the qualification decisions are calibrated on real history (signalman-ufg.6), because remediation compounds every qualification error.
3. A human approval channel exists in incident.io that signalman can wait on (a workflow or decision flow), with the approver, the action and the target written to the incident timeline before anything runs.
4. The action surface is an allow-list of idempotent operations with a dry-run mode, each with its own permission, audit event and OpenTelemetry span (signalman-m28.2).

When reopened, re-evaluate the SDK choice at that time; Cersei's Tool, PermissionPolicy and Hook traits are a reasonable shape for an allow-listed action surface, but its dependency weight and maturity were disqualifying in 2026-09.

Beads sync from the cloud sandbox (2026-09-25): the git proxy allows pushes only to refs/heads/claude/* and refuses refs/dolt/* and branch deletions, so bd dolt push cannot work here; SSH is absent, so sync.remote (git+ssh) is unusable and a local https Dolt remote is needed for bd bootstrap / bd dolt pull (bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/chussenot/signalman.git --allow-git-origin). Harness (signalman-o77): nine agents in .claude/agents. Read-only reviewers/auditors report, writers edit. config-reviewer = the seven places a setting lives (Settings schema, effective struct, resolve, ENV_VARS, unit test, docs/configuration.md row, example TOML / .env.example) plus decision 0006 rules; observability-reviewer = instrument names only in telemetry.rs, service.operation spans on every pub async client method, no bodies/secrets in span fields, docs table and tests/telemetry.rs agree; test-writer = wiremock per upstream, real TcpListener for transports, .expect(n) on writes, footguns (tuple-drop of MockServer, once-per-process globals, multi_thread for blocking exporters, up_to_n_times sequencing); pr-shepherd = PR body shape Summary / Decisions to review / Test plan, CI billing-block signature (runner_id 0, done within ~10 s of created_at, no steps, same on main) and the one standing-down comment; refactor-scout = pub items with no references outside their definition are dead because publish=false, plus duplicates/stale comments/unused deps, ranked by value over risk; docs-auditor = claims vs code with grep, why-gaps per section, links/anchors/last_reviewed/nav/index drift; docs-writer = problem first, then decision, rejected alternative, cost; link ADRs for the why. OpenTelemetry in signalman (m28.2, src/telemetry.rs, docs/observability.md). Crates: opentelemetry/opentelemetry_sdk/opentelemetry-otlp 0.32 with tracing-opentelemetry 0.33 - tracing-opentelemetry numbers releases ONE AHEAD of the opentelemetry crate it depends on (0.33 -> otel 0.32); cargo add of matching numbers fails to resolve. Features: otlp http-proto + reqwest-blocking-client (the SDK default: PeriodicReader and BatchSpanProcessor run on their own std thread and call the exporter with block_on, so the async reqwest client would panic without a runtime; the blocking client is built on a spawned thread inside the SDK); otlp reqwest is 0.13 like ours, no dual tree, no tonic. with_endpoint on the HTTP exporter is used AS-IS (only the env var path appends /v1/traces), so telemetry.rs appends /v1/traces and /v1/metrics itself; OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS is read by the exporter (env-only secret), per-signal endpoint/protocol vars are ignored by design. Providers::init installs registry + EnvFilter + fmt layer (+ otel layer and global meter provider when an endpoint is set); it must run once in main before any span, and Providers::shutdown must run at exit (main does it via spawn_blocking) or a one-shot CLI run exports nothing. Instruments are created lazily from the global meter via telemetry::metrics() (OnceLock) - fine because init precedes first use; in tests without a provider everything is a no-op. Spans: #[tracing::instrument] on client methods (service.operation names), triage/triage.flow on the Triager, webhook.receive per delivery, triage.background follows_from the request span (rendered as a span link). Upstream errors are counted in http::send_with_retries which now takes a service label. tests/telemetry.rs uses wiremock as the OTLP collector (protobuf keeps strings verbatim, so body_string contains checks work) with flavor=multi_thread and shutdown in spawn_blocking. Readiness (m28.3, src/readiness.rs): GET /readyz on the serve router, 200/503 with a JSON Report (ready, checked_at, cached, upstreams[{service, ok, latency_ms, error?}]) and Cache-Control: no-store. Checks are the cheapest authenticated calls: typesafe list_models, incidentio identity, backstage by-query limit 1 (only when a catalog is configured); concurrent via tokio::join, each under server.readiness_timeout_seconds (default 3), report cached server.readiness_cache_seconds (default 30, 0 = every request), failures cached too; a tokio Mutex around the cache serialises concurrent probes. The deadline includes the client retry policy, so a short deadline reports timed out rather than the transport error.
